title: When using LibGodot on Linux the crash handler overwrites native signal handlers if they exist
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: master

### System information

Linux (for sure), Windows with MinGW (possible), macOS (possible)

### Issue description

On Linux `signal(SIGSEGV, handle_crash);` will use the latest set signal handler, which will be Godot's.

I used LibGodot with C#, and C# runtime sets its own signal handlers that are later get overwritten in Godot's initialization. I tried to use `--disable-crash-handler`, but it doesn't restore the previous signal handlers. 

I'm not sure this extends to other platforms, but Windows with MinGW could also be affected... maybe macOS too?

I can think of couple of ways to resolve it:
1. Provide a scons option to always compile Godot with a disabled crash handler, easy to add as Godot already doesn't compile them for release build, so we can reuse the same system. The LibGodot users will then need to check if their language sets signal handlers automatically and can compile Godot with enabled or disabled crash handler depending on the result.
2. Make `--disable-crash-handler` restore previous signal handlers and rely on LibGodot users to manually add `--disable-crash-handler` themselves.
3. Don't initialize crash handler when it detects `--disable-crash-handler` and rely on LibGodot users to manually add `--disable-crash-handler` themselves.
4. Implement signal chaining in crash handler, the hardest option for almost no users.
5. Always disable the crash handler when building for LibGodot. I think not all languages will need or want to disable it, so this option is just here to be here as it still fixes it.

For me C# already needs a custom fork, so I can add changes here myself, but it would be nice to have the issue fixed in the base engine, especially seeing that any fix will touch the core systems or the main build system or the source files on several different platforms.

### Steps to reproduce

Use LibGodot on Linux

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
